title: Finitely presented module tests for universal acyclicity imply K-flatness
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $E^\bullet$ an arbitrary cochain complex of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For an $A$-module $M$, write $M[0]$ for the complex equal to $M$ in degree zero and zero elsewhere, and use the direct-sum total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], specialized to ordinary modules. Suppose $\operatorname{Tot}(E^\bullet\otimes_A M[0])$ is acyclic for every finitely presented $A$-module $M$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Then $E^\bullet$ is K-flat [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. No boundedness or flatness of its individual terms is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0E8F, lemma-universally-acyclic-K-flat, specialized to commutative rings.

proof.text: Filtered colimits of acyclic module complexes are acyclic. The private proved helper acyclic_of_filtered_colimit forms the short complex of functors in degrees r-1,r,r+1, proves its exactness by evaluating at every stage, and applies Mathlib colim.exact_mapShortComplex. ModuleCat.AB supplies exact filtered colimits; AB5OfSize_shrink also supplies the integer-indexed case. This replaces the elementwise cycle calculation by the existing exact-colimit API.

source.place: Tag 0E8F, filtered-colimit reductions; exactness of filtered colimits (Algebra Tag 00DB).

proof.text: For fixed E, use Functor.map₂HomologicalComplex with curriedTensor and its flip. The existing BifunctorColimits instances show that each resulting total-tensor functor preserves colimits because tensoring modules preserves colimits. The single-degree embedding also preserves colimits. All comparisons are isomorphisms of complexes, so the signed differentials are included.

For every module M, apply Module.exists_directed_colimit_finitePresentation [lem-trf-module-finitely-presented-directed-colimit]. Map its colimit cocone through the single-degree embedding and left tensor by E; every stage is acyclic by the hypothesis. Step 1 proves the colimit is acyclic. The cocone vertex is ULift M, and the real isomorphism ULift.moduleEquiv transports the result to M. The private acyclic_of_iso helper transports zero homology along any isomorphism.

The private proved helper acyclic_all_of_single works for a colimit-preserving cochain functor induced by a triangulated functor on the homotopy category. Take the inverse image of subcategoryAcyclic under that functor. It is a triangulated subcategory. HomotopyCategory.mem_subcategory_of_strictly_bounded proves membership for every bounded complex once it holds for its terms in degree zero. The existing source proof performs exactly the shift and degreewise-split brutal-truncation induction of Stacks. Transport membership through the quotient comparison to obtain acyclicity of the image complex. Thus the zero and single-term cases and finite-length induction are supplied by an already proved source declaration, without a separate homology-long-exact-sequence dependency.

source.place: Tag 0E8F, bounded-complex induction using the split brutal-truncation sequence.

proof.text: For a bounded-above L, use L.coconeStupidFiltrationGE and L.isColimitCoconeStupidFiltrationGE, reindexed along Int.opEquivalence.symm. Every stage is a bounded brutal lower truncation, hence its image is acyclic by step 4. Preservation of this colimit and step 1 prove acyclicity of the image of L. No acyclicity of the brutal truncations is required.

source.place: Tag 0E8F, reduction from bounded-above to bounded complexes; Homology Tag 0118.

proof.text: For arbitrary K, use the existing good upper-truncation diagram K.filtrationLE and its colimit cocone K.isColimitFiltrationLECocone. Every truncation K.truncLE j is bounded above, so steps 5, 2 and 1 prove that its image under the functor is acyclic. This proves the stronger assertion that the image of every complex is acyclic.

source.place: Tag 0E8F, reduction by canonical upper truncations; Homology Tag 0118.

proof.text: Apply steps 4-6 first to left tensor by E. For right tensor, obtain the all-module degree-zero hypothesis from step 3 using mapBifunctorSingle₂Iso, the ordinary module braiding (mapped to complexes), and the inverse of mapBifunctorSingle₁Iso. Then apply the same helper to right tensor. Both functors descend to triangulated functors on homotopy categories via bifunctorMapHomotopyCategory. HomotopyCategory.preservesQuasiIso_iff_preserves_acyclic converts their acyclic-image assertions into preservation of quasi-isomorphisms, and Functor.preservesQuasiIso_iff_of_factors transports this to cochain complexes. The conjunction is definitionally quasiIso.kFlat E [def-pc-module-kflat-complex].

source.place: Tag 0E8F, conclusion via the K-flat definition (Tag 06XZ) and tensor symmetry.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0E8F, lemma-universally-acyclic-K-flat. Lean follows its filtered-colimit, bounded-complex, brutal-truncation and canonical-truncation reductions, using the already proved categorical devissage and colimit APIs. Exactness of filtered colimits replaces the elementwise proof; bounded devissage replaces the separate homology-long-exact-sequence call.
